items.title: Why does a deadline give you a knot?
items.text:
Why does a deadline give you a knot?

You feel a knot in your stomach whenever a deadline looms, but ancient hunters and modern scientists say that knot is a relic of a different fight.

Evidence: Hans Selye (1936, Canada): Chronic pressure spikes cortisol by about 15 to 20 percent; Michael Gurven et al. (2015, Tanzania): Hadza average cortisol about 30 percent lower than industrial societies

MindLore: how your mind works, from real research.

#psychology #mindset #Shorts #selfimprovement #MindLore

items.title: Your memory isn't a notebook
items.text:
Your memory isn't a notebook

You think your memory works like a reliable notebook.

Evidence: Hermann Ebbinghaus (1885, Germany): You lose about 58% of new information after 20 minutes; Nelson Cowan (2001, University of Missouri): Working memory holds about four chunks; Michael Gurven (2015, Tanzania): Hadza use landscape memory similar to ancient Greeks

MindLore: how your mind works, from real research.

#psychology #criticalthinking #Shorts #mindset #MindLore

items.title: Why you chase danger
items.text:
Why you chase danger

You feel a jolt of electricity when you skip a turn signal.

Evidence: Richard Lee (1979, Kalahari Desert): San people in the Kalahari spent about 25 hours a week hunting; Robin Dunbar (1990s, Oxford University): Primate and human social bonds are maintained through high-arousal activities
